name: Least-to-Most Prompting
executive_summary: Break a hard problem into an ordered sequence of strictly easier subproblems, then solve them in order, each conditioned on the answers so far.
description: Stage one asks the model to decompose the target problem into a list of simpler subproblems, ordered so each depends only on subproblems already solved. Stage two solves them one at a time, feeding prior subanswers into each subsequent prompt. This targets a specific CoT failure mode: easy-to-hard generalization, where a single chain trained/prompted on easy examples struggles to generalize to harder compositional instances.
when_to_use: The task is compositional — a hard instance is built from a known sequence of easier sub-tasks (e.g. multi-step math word problems, compositional generalization benchmarks).
when_not_to_use: The problem doesn't decompose cleanly into an ordered, dependency-respecting subproblem sequence.
known_pitfalls: Decomposition quality (stage one) bottlenecks everything downstream — a bad decomposition guarantees a bad final answer regardless of stage-two solving quality.

primary_source.authors: Zhou, Schärli, Hou, Wei, Scales, Wang, Schuurmans, Cui, Bousquet, Le, Chi
primary_source.title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models

variables.name: prior_subanswers
variables.description: Running list of subproblem: subanswer pairs solved so far

variables.name: current_subproblem
variables.description: The next subproblem in the decomposition

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
